rendering.persona_description: Pablo is 26 and works as a mechanical design associate at a mid-sized manufacturing firm outside Columbus. He grew up the oldest of three kids in a family where his dad ran a small HVAC business, and he was the first to go to a four-year college. He plays in a weekly pickup basketball league and is fairly particular about keeping his apartment organized, which his roommate finds funny.
rendering.clinical_context: Pablo has ordinary stress and low mood that come and go, tied mostly to periods when work feels uncertain or unrewarding. This has been part of his pattern since his last year of college, flaring around performance reviews, layoff rumors, or stretches where he feels stuck, and easing once things stabilize. It has never risen to a diagnosable episode and he functions normally at work and with friends even during the low stretches.
rendering.behavioral_description: He talks in a fairly direct, slightly understated way, often minimizing how much something is bothering him before admitting it's been on his mind a lot. He'll push back if a suggestion sounds generic or like it's not accounting for his specific situation, and he wants to feel like he's being heard as competent rather than fragile. He sometimes circles back to money and career trajectory even when the conversation starts somewhere else.
